notes.title: PATCH 1.0.2 is here!
notes.content:
1.0.2 Patch Notes

Improvements

 Procedural challenge layouts no longer repeat the same object placement each time.
 Steam Deck resolution list now excludes unintended low-resolution options when using Borderless mode.


Bug Fixes

 “The Architect’s Knowledge” achievement can now be completed. It no longer requires the golden gem that was previously locked behind the achievement itself.
 The “Soda Star” item no longer reduces its own critical bonus damage due to a hidden modifier.
 Bol-Love-Aro achievement now properly tracks item purchases made during challenges.
 Restored the missing text in Bernardo’s dialogue after losing to the Doppelganger.
 Various localization fixes

notes.title: PATCH 1.0.1 is here!
notes.content:
1.0.1 Patch Notes


Improvements

- Reduced enemies' health in Biomes 2 & 3.
- Combo now lasts 2.5s and fades for 1s
- Effects for the following items have been adjusted:

 Real Estate Expert → Entering a hostile room generates [strike]5/10/20/35[/strike] 10/20/30/50 shards
 Certified pyrotechnician → Hitting an enemy with a bomb generates [strike]1/2/3/5[/strike] 3/5/7/10 explosive shards
 Auric Obsession → Grant [strike]1[/strike] 1/2/3/5 gold every [strike]30/25/20/10[/strike] 20 combo points
 Drinkable Gunpowder → Weapon becomes a bomb every [strike]35/30/25/15[/strike] 30/25/20/10 combo points
 Static Electricity → Remain at [strike]40/35/25/10[/strike] 20/15/10/5 combo points, weapon attacks generate electric arcs
 Weaponsmith Expert → As long as you remain at 10+ combo points, generate [strike]2[/strike] 5 shards every [strike]1s[/strike] 3/2.5/2/1s
 Shattered heart → Weapon generates shard every [strike]0.25s[/strike] 0.2s

- Echo dice effects now trigger directly when interacting with “heart” items such as Infernal Heart.
- New icons added for the patterns to make them easier to understand.
- Various improvements and fixes for some of the Experiences.

Bug Fixes

- Patterns can no longer be farmed indefinitely.
- Bomb Room description no longer claims to grant control.
- Doors in the 2nd Biome no longer unexpectedly lock players behind them.
- Fixed issue where the Doppelganger unlock sequence dialog triggered too early.
- Removed lag caused by Echo Device + Electricity
- Potion "Hazardous Duplicator" no longer grants common versions of items that were unintended.
- Boss achievements unlock correctly if defeated without taking any hits.
- Fixed issue preventing the Bo-Love-Aro achievement from unlocking correctly.
- Addressed problem where the quality control item appeared incorrectly in Act 1.
- Fixed card VFX not displaying properly during ACT unlocking sequences.
- Rotten Egg gives the correct amount of empty hearts for each curse.
- Bernardo's Codex entry has been restored in English.
- Codex entries are no longer cut off in Spanish.
- Character names are correctly translated in certain languages.
- Various localization fixes in all languages.

1.0.1

notes.title: Cryptical Path Release Update
notes.content:
Greetings, adventurers! 🗺️⚔️

We’re thrilled to officially announce that Cryptical Path, the first-ever Roguelite Builder, is coming!

Originally set for winter 2024, Cryptical Path will now be released in early 2025.

This journey has been all about crafting an epic roguelike experience where you don’t just survive the dungeon—you build it. With the Hexium Map, intense battles, and endless strategies to explore, we can’t wait for you to dive in and start forging your path.

The team is hard at work polishing the game to ensure it’s everything you’re hoping for—and more. Your patience and support mean the world to us, and we promise it’ll be worth the wait.

Stay tuned for more updates, sneak peeks, and devlogs as we get closer to launch. And don’t forget to wishlist Cryptical Path to be notified the moment it’s available!

Thank you for being part of this adventure. See you in the dungeon!

🏴‍☠️ The Old Skull Games Team

notes.title: How did we approach replayability ?
notes.content:
Introduction

Hey everyone, I’m Jérémy, Game Director for Cryptical Path. I'm excited to walk you through our approach to replayability in the game, which happens to be the focus point of this week's fest.
Of course, Cryptical Path is an action rogue-lite, and this means a lot in terms of replay value. That's why I'm going to dive into some aspects of the game that influenced us during the design process and that I think had an impact on this particular subject. We've always aimed for the game to be highly replayable, as it is a characteristic of rogue games.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678730/4537a336d2957dd3059f63f9980dd4536116b089.png

Unique combinations of items in every Run:
When crafting the game's items, our primary focus was ensuring that each playthrough offered a unique experience for the player. This involved creating items capable of altering gameplay dynamics and fostering synergies between seemingly basic components. While not every item is intended to be a game-changer on its own, the combination of several can yield unexpected results.
For instance, consider the combination of an item that reduces spell cooldowns with another that enables spells to generate echo dice. This synergy completely transforms gameplay dynamics, allowing players to utilize their dice from a considerable distance using spells.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678730/d3dcf9b8eed9ba4169a7a3121fa7448e151f4f1d.gif

The Hexium Map:
This main feature adds a layer of complexity to the game, and offers choices in the gameplay. It's truly something that can enhance replayability as each run can be different based on how you use it.
We believe the Hexium map is more than just a tool, it's a versatile feature designed to empower players to tailor their gameplay experience to their preferences. This innovative approach not only helps players in adapting to the unpredictability of random generation but also serves as a means to dynamically alter the challenges they encounter in each run.

This feature is truly what sets our game apart, offering players the ability to strategically place rooms and regain control over their experience, mitigating the potential drawbacks of randomness.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678730/cc4407497df1a002bfd19d607cfd5e9d6ef9b6e2.gif

Challenges and Difficulty Modes:
Replaying a level is only enjoyable when it's inherently fun to play. We firmly believe that players should find genuine enjoyment in the core gameplay experience before considering replayability. However, merely offering different items, rooms and enemies each run isn't sufficient. Introducing varied objectives also motivates players to retry and replay until they achieve success, thereby providing them with a gratifying sense of accomplishment. This principle lies at the heart of rogue games, often rendering them challenging to complete.

In Cryptical Path, we've designed different modes that go beyond simple difficulty levels like easy, medium, or hard. Instead, these modes progressively escalate the complexity of the game, offering players a deeper and more nuanced experience rather than just balanced difficulty levels.

Engaging Progression:
As our game is a roguelite, we've incorporated progression systems to assist players along their journey. By implementing these systems, we can introduce more complex features gradually, ensuring a smoother onboarding process and avoiding overwhelming players right from the start. These systems take the form of a talent tree, achievement system, and unlockable items.

While these features may not directly enhance replayability, they serve as compelling reasons for players to start the game. Unlocking cool new items and experimenting with different playstyles adds depth and variety to each playthrough, encouraging players to approach the game in unique ways every time while having something to achieve.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678730/6618fddeec0886c4a736a55df45244610a127ff3.gif

Balancing Run Length:
One of the most challenging aspects of designing Cryptical Path was finding the right balance between punishment and progression. Each run needed to be sufficiently lengthy to feel unique, yet not excessively so that losing felt overly harsh. That is also why we decided to implement the progression systems that we talked before, it helps having short runs at the beginning, and make them last longer as a player progresses through the game.

That's all for now, enjoy the Endless Replayability Fest!

notes.title: Demo Update: Take the Tour
notes.content:
Hi Architects, 

As we prepare for the Steam Next Fest period, we are releasing a new demo with several improvements. These include a brand new weapon to help you navigate the dungeon, balancing fixes, and an enhanced onboarding experience for newcomers. Take a look at the complete list below:

Main Changes
New weapon: the Dice. The Architect is now carrying a brand new weapon that replaces the old one: the dice. Roll it and meet your destiny. 10 New items comes with the dice, creating new possibilities for synergy and massive destructions.
By popular demand, we added invincibility frames on dash
We’ve worked on an improved onboarding experience to allow newcomers to start their journey in the dungeon more easily
Progression 

 You can now collect frozen souls during your run to spend in your hub
 You can now access the Hub and meet Bernardo
 You can purchase new items to find in your future runs 
 You can unlock new rooms to use on the board
 Fixes and polish to increase overhaul immersion and correct multiple issues.

Board 

 Art and FX have been reworked to make board more clear & readable
 When the board is locked (-10 controls) path is now created leading to the boss and raising the difficulty to its maximum instead of giving the ability to teleport to the boss room.

Balancing

 Difficulty of visited rooms increases overtime
 Changed the price of rooms you can place 
 You start the game with 5 hearts (was 3)
 You start the game with 10 control (was 5)
 Boss has New attack patterns
 Boss attacks order patterns is now random


Have a suggestion for more improvements? Join the Cryptical Path Community on Discord and share your ideas in the server.

notes.title: The Art of Cryptical Path
notes.content:
The work on the art of Cryptical Path has been a hell of a roller coaster, and we sat down with Laura Maetz, Rudy Wilde and Cédric Cadiergues to learn about this art journey and their inspirations for the game.

Inspirations

Cryptical path is the culmination of extensive work and multiple attempts to discover the ideal setting for this innovative roguelite. Early on, the team decided on things they didn’t want for the game: everything too scary was pushed aside, inspirations like Little Nightmares or Coraline who would be too on the scary side for example.

The team wanted to find a sweet spot between spooky and gloomy, without a cartoonish aspect, and draw inspiration from games like Lost in Random™ but also from dark fantasy and RP games to incorporate elements that would add to the mystery and dark ambiance.

When working on inspirations, Cédric Cadiergues explains that the appropriate artistic direction for Cryptical Path was also determined by analyzing the team's abilities in detail (number of people in the team, skills and time), a crucial preliminary work for any indie team.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678730/59ed68fef6d59a84fbcda4553f8c63556f9f2c24.png
Screenshot of Lost in Random™, by Zoink Games

The Architect

Locked in a prison called The Hexium, the main character, the Architect, builds their own path through the dungeon. "Because it's a prison, the space is unstructured and props become threatening," explains Cédric Cadiergues, Art Director, who enjoys working on the environment and lighting in the game, among other things.

According to Rudy Wilde, "The goal for the Architect was to create a non-human character: a creature or a demon, a cursed being." Many proposals were made before the current version of the Architect, some even more complex! They draw inspiration from many different models and cultures, even voodoo imagery.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678730/5ba304559d3fbbea2bf4967d1c4bfc4b2baf0849.png

A dangerous dungeon

Early on, enemies, mobs, and bosses were based on props: cursed objects found in the dungeon that would become foes in the Architect's way. This concept remained unchanged from the beginning and continues to this day. In a cursed setting, the idea of a twisted reality with moving (and frankly mean) objects to challenge the player made sense from the start.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678730/21b17bbc1504d6361066d635df3897648c4f136f.png

Rudy Wilde alongside Laura Maetz have put a lot of effort into designing the various bosses that players will have to face, and creating character's design that captures their power and timing. “Working on conveying the difficulty through the art is hands down my favorite part”, shared Laura.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678730/573348da457cb7d0863f99be8a82287ad4d951ac.png

A constance: Bernardo

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678730/3729038b30c309a6e36209417a387568b22288ec.png

Bernardo "survived" every iteration of the game and its art. Since he was crafted right from the start to be a very funny character, his design and quirky tone remained consistent throughout the process, making him a very fun and adaptable figure in the game. He was born from a sweet mix between two references: Gaunter o’Dim from The Witcher 3 and a drawing from the artwork of American experimental rock band Mr Bungle’s first album.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678730/e5bf8455fd3d8913e3987fb534a3905bfd9f5b36.png

What to expect

Cryptical Path will include different biomes, all inspired by a setting in particular. You can already discover the first biome in the demo, based on a foggy manor-like maze. If you like the game and its rogue builder experience, please add it to your wishlist!

Do you like the art of Cryptical Path? Did it inspire you in any way? If you are making fan art, don’t hesitate to join the community on Discord and share your creations!
